newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds edge lower, dollar mixed.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds edge lower, dollar mixed.

text.p: Stocks edged lower Thursday as investors took profits, bonds fell and the dollar ended mixed.
Gold tumbled to its lowest level in 20 months. Oil rose.

After setting November's 10th record high on Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average slipped 11.55 points to 6,418.47. In the broader market, advancing issues edged declines, 1,198 to 1,195, on heavy volume of about 468.7 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"After the feeding frenzy of the past couple of weeks, investors are taking a bit of a breather here. There's a bit of profit-taking, nothing dramatic," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell.
The Nasdaq composite index lost 6.86 points to 1,258.08 as heavyweights Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp. gave up some of their recent strong gains.

"It looks like we're making a bit of a pitstop. Some profit-taking has kicked in but by and large the tilt appears to be up. There appears to be some nervousness about the market's big move over the past 10 days," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.
One focus for investors was temporary staffing companies. "That's all related to Olsten," said Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst.

Olsten Corp., the most-active NYSE issue, tumbled 5-1/2 points to 14-3/8 after forecasting fourth-quarter earnings will fall well below expectations. It cited ongoing competitive pressures at its two main businesses and lower revenues from Medicare operations.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 4/32, or $1.25 on a $1,000 bond, raising the yield to 6.42 percent from 6.41 percent at Wednesday's close.
The dollar fell to 111.27 Japanese yen late in New York from 111.55 yen late on Wednesday. But it rose to 1.4980 German marks from 1.4965.

The mark fell to a 31-month low against the British pound and slid to its lowest level against the Italian lira in a month. The pound rose to a fresh four-year high against the dollar, ending at $1.6890, up from $1.6820 Wednesday.
Gold prices fell on selling by mining companies and U.S.-based investment funds.
On New York's Commodity Exchange, December gold lost $2.50 an ounce to $376.50, just above an earlier new life-of-contract low of $375.80.
January crude oil rose 51 cents to $23.84 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index fell 9 points to 3,953.8. In Tokyo, the key Nikkei 225 finished at 21,143.34, down 46.62 points.
